'''Aaron Malik Harrison''' (born October 28, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Diablos Rojos del México (basketball)|Diablos Rojos del México]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]] (LNBP). He was considered one of the top high school recruits in 2013 and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]] alongside his twin brother [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rankin |first1=Reggie |last2=Telep |first2=Dave |date=October 5, 2012 |title=Harrison twins choose Kentucky |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8462850 |access-date=May 20, 2023 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Raphielle|last=Johnson|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2012/10/04/2013-guards-aaron-and-andrew-harrison-verbally-commit-to-attend-kentucky/|title=2013 guards Aaron and Andrew Harrison verbally commit to attend Kentucky|work=NBCSports.com|date=October 4, 2012|access-date=October 4, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Larry|last=Vaught|url=http://articles.centralkynews.com/2013-04-10/amnews/38442827_1_aaron-harrison-state-championship-travis-high-school|title=Vaught's Views: Aaron Harrison shows he is a special player, like his twin brother|work=CentralKYNews.com|date=April 10, 2013|access-date=April 10, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112112414/http://articles.centralkynews.com/2013-04-10/amnews/38442827_1_aaron-harrison-state-championship-travis-high-school|archive-date=November 12, 2013}}</ref>
Harrison played in both the [[Jordan Brand Classic#2013|2013 Jordan Brand Classic]], and the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Steve |last=Jones |url=http://blogs.courier-journal.com/recruiting/2013/04/04/andrew-harrison-recaps-mcdonalds-game/ |title=Andrew Harrison recaps McDonald's game |work=Courier-Journal.com |date=April 4, 2013 |access-date=April 4, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130615063232/http://blogs.courier-journal.com/recruiting/2013/04/04/andrew-harrison-recaps-mcdonalds-game/ |archive-date=June 15, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Colleen|last=Kane|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2013/03/31/kentucky-recruits-dominate-mcdonalds-all-american-game-rosters/|title=Kentucky recruits dominate McDonald's All-American game rosters|work=ChicagoTribune.com|date=March 31, 2013|access-date=March 31, 2013}}</ref>

==High school career==
[[File:20130403 MCDAAG Aaron Harrison defending Wayne Selden.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Harrison defending against [[Wayne Selden]] in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
Harrison was widely regarded as a top five player in the class of 2013 with [[Andrew Wiggins]], [[Jabari Parker]], [[Julius Randle]], and twin brother [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew]]. On March 9, 2013, Harrison and his brother, Andrew, helped the Fort Bend Travis Tigers to defeat South Grand Prairie, 46–38 at the Frank Erwin Center on the campus of the University of Texas at Austin to win the Class 5A state title in Texas. They finished #16 in the final ESPN 25 Power Rankings. Fort Bend Travis had lost in the Class 5A state title game the year before to Flower Mound Marcus.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/powerrankings?week=99&season=2012|title=ESPN 25 Power Rankings: Final|work=ESPN.com|access-date=May 18, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Brandon|last=Parker|url= https://www.espn.com/blog/high-school/texas/tag/_/name/fort-bend-travis/fort-bend-travis-tigers-defeated-by-flower-mound-marcus-the-year-before|title=Texas final hoops rankings: FM Marcus, Kimball repeat as champs|work=ESPN.com|date=March 13, 2012|access-date=May 18, 2023}}</ref> He also was the Guy V. Lewis Award winner in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://guyvlewisaward.org/|title=The Guy V. Lewis Award|accessdate=June 25, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
Harrison started at [[shooting guard]] in all 40 games for the University of Kentucky during the [[2013–14 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2013–14 season]], averaging 13.7 points with 42.3% shooting, 35.6% 3-point shooting, and 79% free throw shooting. He scored a career-high 28 points against [[Robert Morris Colonials men's basketball|Robert Morris]] on November 17, 2013, all while shooting a perfect 10-of-10 from the free throw line. On March 30, 2014, Harrison hit a game-winning three-point field goal versus [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] in the regional finals of the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2014 NCAA Men's Division I basketball tournament]]. On April 5, 2014, Harrison hit a game-winning three-pointer versus [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] in the semi-finals of the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. He finished the game with 8 points, all coming in the second half.

On April 25, 2014, Harrison and his brother both announced via [[Twitter]] that they would return to play their sophomore years at the University of Kentucky, instead of entering the [[2014 NBA draft]].

Prior to the start of the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 season]], Harrison was named the preseason [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Lintner|url=http://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-kentucky/2014/10/22/kentucky-wildcats-basketball-picked-to-win-sec/17732167/|title=UK picked to win SEC; Aaron Harrison player of year|work=Cincinnati.com|date=September 22, 2014|access-date = October 26, 2014}}</ref>

On April 9, 2015, Harrison declared for the [[2015 NBA draft|NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility. He was joined alongside his twin brother Andrew and fellow Kentucky teammates [[Karl-Anthony Towns]], [[Willie Cauley-Stein]], [[Trey Lyles]], [[Devin Booker]], and [[Dakari Johnson]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Timothy|last=Rapp|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2424123-andrew-aaron-harrison-to-declare-for-2015-nba-draft-latest-details-reaction|title=Andrew, Aaron Harrison to Declare for 2015 NBA Draft: Latest Details, Reaction|work=BleacherReport|publisher=Bleacher Report|date=April 8, 2015|access-date=April 10, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Charlotte Hornets (2015–2017)===
After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], Harrison joined the [[Charlotte Hornets]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-announce-2015-orlando-pro-summer-league-roster |title=Hornets Announce 2015 Orlando Pro Summer League Roster|last=Wash|first=Quinton|work=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2015|access-date=May 18, 2023}}</ref> On July 14, 2015, he signed with the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-sign-free-agent-guard-aaron-harrison|title=Hornets Sign Free Agent Guard Aaron Harrison|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2015 |last=Wash|first=Quinton|access-date=May 18, 2023}}</ref> He made his NBA debut on November 20, 2015, recording one rebound in two minutes of action against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref name=br>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/harriaa01/gamelog/2016/|title=Aaron Harrison 2015–16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 21, 2016}}</ref> In the Hornets' regular season finale on April 13, 2016, Harrison had a season-best game with six points and five rebounds in a 117–103 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref name="br" /> During his rookie season, using the flexible assignment rule, Harrison received multiple assignments to the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] and the [[Osceola Magic|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 7, 2016|archive-date=March 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Over the first two months of the 2016–17 season, Harrison spent much of his time in the D-League with Charlotte's new affiliate, the [[Greensboro Swarm]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016–17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 7, 2016|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 3, 2017, he was waived by the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web |last=Ramirez |first=Miguel |date=January 3, 2017 |title=Charlotte Hornets Waive Guard Aaron Harrison |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/charlotte-hornets-waive-guard-aaron-harrison |access-date=May 18, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Greensboro Swarm (2017)===
On January 15, 2017, Harrison was acquired by the Greensboro Swarm<ref>{{cite web|first=Dennis|last=Varney|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/ex-cats/article126712794.html|title=D-League's Greensboro Swarm add Aaron Harrison to roster|work=Kentucky.com|publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader|date=January 15, 2017|access-date=January 15, 2017}}</ref> making his debut that day in a 105–95 loss to the [[Iowa Energy]], recording four points, four rebounds and two assists in 17 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20170115/GBOIWA/|title=Selden Pours In 30 As Energy Top Swarm|work=NBA.com|date=January 15, 2017|access-date=January 15, 2017|archive-date=January 18, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118190300/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20170115/GBOIWA/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Delaware 87ers (2017)===
On February 3, 2017, Harrison was traded to the [[Delaware 87ers]] in exchange for [[Cat Barber]] and the returning player rights to [[Sam Thompson (basketball)|Sam Thompson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/release-sevens-acquire-aaron-harrison/|title=SEVENS ACQUIRE AARON HARRISON|work=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2017|access-date=February 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170203225612/http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/release-sevens-acquire-aaron-harrison/|archive-date=February 3, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Reno Bighorns (2017–2018)===
On November 3, 2017, Harrison, together with some draft picks, was traded to the [[Reno Bighorns]] in exchange for returning player rights to [[Kendall Marshall]] and [[Youssou Ndoye]] and a draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=BIGHORNS COMPLETE TWO TRADES PRIOR TO SEASON TIP-OFF – Reno Bighorns|url=http://reno.gleague.nba.com/news/bighorns-complete-two-trades-prior-season-tip-off/|last=Jones|first=Kyle|website=gleague.nba.com|access-date=March 22, 2018|archive-date=March 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323034257/http://reno.gleague.nba.com/news/bighorns-complete-two-trades-prior-season-tip-off/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2018)===
On March 22, 2018, Harrison signed a 10-day contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Mavericks sign Aaron Harrison to 10-day contract|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-aaron-harrison-10-day-contract/|last=Karalla |first=Bobby|website=mavs.com|access-date=March 22, 2018|date=March 22, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323092256/https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-aaron-harrison-10-day-contract/|archive-date=March 23, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> and on March 31, after playing four games, he signed with the Mavericks for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Aaron Harrison signs rest-of-season deal with Mavs|url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/aaron_harrison_signs_rest_of_season_deal_with_mavs/s1_14822_26089010|website=yardbarker.com|access-date=April 2, 2018|date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> He did not receive a qualifying offer from the Mavericks after the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/06/30/free-agency-contract-options-qualifying-offers|title=Guide to 2018 contract options, qualifying offers|work=nba.com|date=June 30, 2018|access-date=June 30, 2018}}</ref>

===Galatasaray (2018–2020)===
On September 5, 2018, Harrison signed with [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Galatasaray signs Aaron Harrison |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/287596/galatasaray-signs-aaron-harrison.html |website=Sportando |access-date=September 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180905175551/https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/287596/galatasaray-signs-aaron-harrison.html |archive-date=September 5, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On August 7, 2019, Harrison renewed his contract with the Turkish club for two (1+1) more seasons.<ref>{{cite web|title=Aaron Harrison ile sözleşme uzatıldı|language=TR|url=https://www.galatasaray.org/haber/basketbol/erkek-basketbol/aaron-harrison-ile-sozlesme-uzatildi/44604|date=August 7, 2019|website=galatasaray.org|access-date=August 7, 2019}}</ref> He averaged 12.8 points, 3.3 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 1.8 steals per game in 2019–20.<ref>{{cite news |last=Varney |first=Dennis |title=Catch up with 36 ex-Cats playing pro basketball in leagues outside the NBA |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/ex-cats/article241420196.html |access-date=May 16, 2020 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=March 26, 2020}}</ref>

===Olympiacos (2020–2021)===
On July 8, 2020, Harrison signed with Greek club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/aaron-harrison-signs-two-year-deal-with-olympiacos/|title=Aaron Harrison signs two-year deal with Olympiacos|date=July 8, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 8, 2020|last=Lupo |first=Nicola }}</ref>

===Türk Telekom (2021–2022)===
On July 16, 2021, Harrison signed with [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]] of the Turkish [[Basketball Super League]]. Türk Telekom also plays as newcomer in the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/TurkTelekom_SK/status/1416117478971912201|title=Türk Telekom signs with Aaron Harrison |date=July 16, 2021|publisher=Twitter (Türk Telekom)| language=Tr |access-date=July 17, 2021}}</ref>

===Cedevita Olimpija (2022)===
On September 15, 2022, Harrison signed with [[KK Cedevita Olimpija|Cedevita Olimpija]] of the [[Premier A Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cedevita-olimpija-ljubljana-signs-aaron-harrison/|title=Cedevita Olimpija Ljubljana signs Aaron Harrison|date=September 15, 2022|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=October 28, 2022|last=Maggi |first=Alessandro }}</ref>

===Kaohsiung Steelers (2022–2023)===
On December 3, 2022, Harrison signed with [[Kaohsiung Steelers]] of the [[P. League+]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/aaron-harrison-joins-kaohsiung-steelers/|title=Aaron Harrison joins Kaohsiung Steelers|date=December 3, 2022|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=December 6, 2022|last=Skerletic |first=Dario }}</ref> On February 6, 2023, his contract was terminated.<ref>{{cite web |title=鋼鐵人向NBA資歷洋將說Thank You 鑀倫無緣再合體林書豪 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2434773 |publisher=ETtoday |access-date=3 November 2024 |date=6 February 2023}}</ref>

===Puerto Rican (2023)===
On January 24, 2023, Harrison signed with [[Capitanes de Arecibo]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN).<ref>{{cite web |title=Arecibo signs Aaron Harrison, ex Steelers |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Taiwan/news/790184/Arecibo-signs-Aaron-Harrison,-ex-Steelers |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=3 November 2024 |date=24 January 2023}}</ref> On April 27, he was replaced by [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Capitanes pactan con Thomas Robinson |url=https://capitanesarecibo.com/2023/04/capitanes-pactan-con-thomas-robinson/ |publisher=Capitanes de Arecibo |access-date=3 November 2024 |date=27 April 2023}}</ref> On April 30, he signed with [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=De Roa |first1=Alberto |title=Former Hornets player Aaron Harrison signed with Puerto Rican team Indios de Mayaguez for the 2023 season. |url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/2030755/ |publisher=HoopsHype |access-date=3 November 2024 |date=30 April 2023}}</ref>

===FC Porto (2023–2024)===
On October 12, 2023, Harrison signed with [[FC Porto (basketball)|FC Porto]] of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol]] (LPB).<ref>{{cite web |title=Aaron Harrison é reforço para o basquetebol |url=https://www.fcporto.pt/pt/noticias/20231011-pt-aaron-harrison-e-reforco-para-o-basquetebol |publisher=FC Porto |access-date=3 November 2024 |date=12 October 2023}}</ref>

===Diablos Rojos del México (2024)===
On September 14, 2024, Harrison signed with [[Diablos Rojos del México (basketball)|Diablos Rojos del México]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]] (LNBP).<ref>{{cite web |title=Aaron Harrison signs with Diablos Rojos in Mexico |url=https://www.nationofblue.com/aaron-harrison-signs-with-diablos-rojos-in-mexico/ |publisher=Nation of Blue |access-date=3 November 2024 |date=14 September 2024}}</ref>
